newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain truck strikers resume talks with government.
newsitem.headline: Spain truck strikers resume talks with government.

text.p: The organisation leading a Spanish truckers strike resumed talks with the government for a second day on Sunday to press demands for improved labour conditions and lower fuel prices.
Spanish Foreign Minister Abel Matutes said the government would adopt measures to avert economic paralysis if the crippling 11-day-old strike was not called off.

"In every situation we must seek an equilibrium between the right to strike and the right of the majority not to be harmed by the interests, no matter how legitimate, of a small minority which in no case has the right to paralyse Spain," he said.
Matutes, who is not directly involved in the negotiations, was speaking to reporters at Madrid's Barajas airport upon his return from a trip to southeast Asia.
Fedatrans, the group spearheading the strike, is demanding truckers be permitted to retire at 60 instead of 65 in addition to recognition of professional illnesses and curbs on surging fuel prices.

The strike has blocked roads and ports and disrupted the supply of goods to parts of northern Spain, forcing some carmakers and other factories to cut back or halt production. It has also been peppered with violence.
